organizations.publicNote: German recording company active from 1925 to 1972; the linked discs use Electrola as their imprint. In 1972 Electrola-Gesellschaft and Carl Lindström GmbH were merged into the successor company EMI Electrola. The designation E.G. belongs to a record series, not to the organization’s name.

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Leo Moll. “Spiel’ mir auf der Balalaika einen russischen Tango.” Electrola E.G. 2392, matrix 00499-1; recorded in Berlin, 18 August 1931, released October 1931; also issued as His Master’s Voice AM 3741. Session and issue data from the Electrola label list at musiktiteldb.de, based on the Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik. Digital transfer on YouTube, video Oq4sWv9khw4.
sources.title: Electrola E.G. 2392
sources.creator: Marek Weber und sein Orchester; Leo Moll, vocal refrain
sources.researchNote: The transfer description dates the recording to 1932, whereas the Electrola label list gives a Berlin session on 18 August 1931 and an October 1931 release. The session-based chronology is preferred.

Digital transfer published on YouTube by 78rpm Musik on 27 April 2025; discographic data from the Electrola label list at musiktiteldb.de.

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain credited as Leo Moll. “Signorina aus Brioni.” Tango; label credits Fritz Rotter and Dr. Kaper for music and text. Electrola E.G. 2400, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube.

sources.researchNote: The uploader identifies the singer credited as Leo Moll as Leo Monosson, gives 1931 as the issue year and accompanies the transfer with a 1930 photograph of Brioni. These details are not printed on the filmed label.

sources.fullCitation: Marek Weber und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Siegfried Arno. “Ach, Otto, Otto…!” Foxtrot; Electrola EG 2135, matrix BD 9264-2, playing time 3:12; recorded in the Beethoven-Saal, Berlin, and released in January 1931; also issued as His Master’s Voice AM 3450. sources.shortCitation: Electrola EG 2228, “Ich steh’ im Schnee und wart’ auf Dich” (Mitja Nikisch with Paul Dorn, 1931)
sources.fullCitation: Mitja Nikisch und sein Orchester, refrain sung by Paul Dorn. “Ich steh’ im Schnee und wart’ auf Dich.” Foxtrot from Die grosse Attraktion. Electrola E.G. 2228, matrix OD106-2, recorded Berlin, 15 March 1931; also issued as His Master’s Voice AM 3411 and R 14602. Electrola label and title lists at musiktiteldb.de, following the Discographie der deutschen Tanzmusik, vol. 4.
sources.title: Ich steh’ im Schnee und wart’ auf Dich — Electrola EG 2228
sources.creator: Mitja Nikisch und sein Orchester; Paul Dorn, refrain vocal
sources.researchNote: The discographic entry assigns both words and music to Bronisław Kaper. The published sheet music instead credits music to Kaper and Walter Jurmann and words to Fritz Rotter and Armin Robinson; the discographic entry is not used to replace those work-level credits.
